prompt: Implement rle_encode and rle_decode in /work/rle.h (C++17, header only), a run-length codec. The encoded string is a sequence of runs. Each run is a decimal count (at least 1, no leading zeros) followed by one character: "aaab" encodes to "3a1b", and 12 'x' characters encode to "12x". rle_encode(s) always writes maximal runs, so it never writes two adjacent runs of the same character; it throws std::invalid_argument if s contains a digit '0'-'9'. rle_decode(s) is the inverse and accepts adjacent runs of the same character ("2a3a" decodes to "aaaaa"). It throws std::invalid_argument if s is not a valid encoding: a run with no count, a count with no character after it, a count of 0, or a count with a leading zero. The empty string encodes and decodes to the empty string. The visible tests are run with: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -o /tmp/t test_rle.cpp && /tmp/t
